title: Nosocomial Outbreaks
paragraphs: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) affect approximately 1 in 10 patients worldwide, causing significant morbidity, mortality, and economic strain on healthcare systems. Nosocomial outbreaks driven by person-to-person transmitted pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2, Clostridioides difficile, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and MRSA generate the most acute clinical and operational crises: triggering staff shortages, ward closures, and delayed procedures. Current control measures rely on broad testing and isolation protocols, but effective intervention requires identifying the specific drivers of an outbreak: such as patient zero, superspreaders, transmission routes, and undetected or imported cases.

NosoTrack is an outbreak analytics platform that infers who infected whom in near real-time by integrating data from hospital Electronic Health Records with Bluetooth enabled contact tracing. It delivers early warnings and actionable reports, enabling hospital Infection Prevention Teams to devise targeted interventions promptly before an outbreak escalates.

platform.title: How It Works
platform.subtitle: NosoTrack integrates various data streams into a unified Bayesian analytics engine that infers transmission chains in near real-time.

cards.title: DNA/RNA Sequencing
cards.desc: Pathogen genomes provide phylogenetic signal for transmission inference.

cards.title: Contact Tracing
cards.desc: Bluetooth-enabled sensors record contacts between patients and staff.

cards.title: Electronic Health Records
cards.desc: EHR provide information on admission & discharge dates, ward assignments, and test results.

anonymisation.title: Data Anonymisation
anonymisation.desc: Patient identifiers are stripped, hashed, and encrypted before analysis, ensuring full GDPR compliance.

engine.title: Transmission Tree Inference
engine.desc: NosoTrack uses Bayesian inference to probabilistically reconstruct transmission trees (who infected whom).

features.desc: Identifies cases imported outside the hospital.

features.desc: Characterises transmission patterns between wards, staff and patients.

earlyWarning.title: Early Warning System
earlyWarning.desc: Real-time alerts and reports are dispatched to Infection Prevention Teams with suggested intervention strategies based on current transmission dynamics.

title: Methods & Software
research.intro: NosoTrack builds on over a decade of research in outbreak reconstruction, focusing on the integration of epidemiological, genomic and contact data to infer transmission trees. Our team and collaborators have published extensively on methodological advances, including the outbreaker2 R package and the linktree method for inferring transmission patterns between staff and patients. These methods have been applied to real outbreak data, including SARS-CoV-2 nosocomial outbreaks in Switzerland, MRSA in neonatal intensive care units in the UK, Klebsiella pneumoniae in a Nepali neonatal unit, Acinetobacter baumannii in hospitals in North Carolina, and Ebola outbreaks in the DRC. We are committed to open science, with all software freely available and publications accessible to the public.

timeline.description: Integrates genetic and epidemiological data using an SEIR model for transmission; assumes complete bottleneck and all cases observed/sampled; inference via maximum likelihood.
Reconstructs transmission trees from genetic data using a graph approach; minimizes total genetic distance; no explicit transmission model.
Bayesian method using mutations; SEIR transmission model with spatial kernel; single introduction.
Bayesian reconstruction combining epidemiologic and genomic data; SI transmission model; handles multiple introductions and sampled cases.
Simultaneous inference in BEAST framework; coalescent process; SEIR model with spatial kernel.
Uses likelihood ratio test for time of most recent common ancestor; Poisson mutation model; no explicit transmission model.
Bayesian method in R package; coalescent process; SI model; handles ongoing outbreaks and proportion of sampled cases.
Simultaneous inference in R package; coalescent process; SI model; all cases observed but not always sampled.
Labels internal nodes in phylogenetic tree; weak bottleneck; no explicit transmission model.
Reconstructs phylogenetic tree from transmission tree; Jukes-Cantor model; all cases observed and sampled.

Bayesian framework combining genomic and epidemiological data using outbreaker2 to reconstruct transmission trees in a nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 outbreak; assesses limits of genomics for outbreak reconstruction.
Combined retrospective epidemiological and genomic study using outbreaker2 to reconstruct transmission chains of SARS-CoV-2 amidst multiple outbreaks in a geriatric acute-care hospital.

Uses a Bayesian framework to infer transmission pairs by exploring all compatible transmission trees based on symptom dates, incorporating a wide range of incubation period and generation time distributions; derives serial intervals from reconstructed pairs, stratified by variants, to account for negative serial intervals.

A framework to estimate group transmission assortativity from transmission chain data, quantifying the extent of within-group vs. between-group transmissions while accounting for group sizes and depletion of susceptibles; implemented in an R package.

A statistical framework implemented in the R package mixtree to compare epidemic forests (collections of plausible transmission trees) using chi-square test and PERMANOVA for detecting differences in transmission dynamics.

members.name: Dr Cyril Geismar
members.bio: Postdoctoral research fellow. PhD in mathematical modelling of infectious diseases at Imperial College London, focused on SARS-CoV-2 outbreak reconstruction. Executive board member and developer for the R Epidemics Consortium. Teaches outbreak analytics at Emory University and LSHTM.

members.name: Dr Thibaut Jombart
members.bio: Senior Lecturer specialising in outbreak response analytics, biostatistics, population genetics, and R programming. Lead author of outbreaker and founder of the R Epidemics Consortium. Field experience in Ebola deployments in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

members.name: Dr Anne Cori
members.bio: Senior Lecturer specialising in real-time outbreak analysis and epidemiological parameters. Lead author of EpiEstim and co-author of outbreaker. Develops statistical methods for outbreak reconstruction and rapid transmissibility assessment.

members.name: Dr Shaun Truelove
members.bio: Associate Professor focused on infectious disease dynamics and modelling for public health response and policy (COVID-19, influenza, vaccine-preventable diseases). Co-leads the US Scenario Modeling Hubs and ACCIDA, a consortium producing epidemic scenario projections and forecasts.
